result.summary: Independently re-verified TEST-DESIGNER's step-12 PASS. (1) Targeted tests: `mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/migration_replay_boot_test.exs` against HEAD 6766956a -> 'Finished in 22.9 seconds' / 'Result: 23 passed', 0 failures, run by me directly -- matches TEST-DESIGNER's claim exactly. Cross-checked all 5 ISS-0771 acceptance criteria (idempotent no-op, per-tenant isolation, real pending-migration replay, start_link/1 always :ignore, healthy-path summary logging) against test/specs/ISS-0771.md and the test file bodies: each has a real, runnable, non-skipped test (grep for `@tag :skip`/`TODO` in both test files and the spec: zero hits). Fixtures use `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` with unique slug prefixes and self-contained `on_exit/1` teardown -- no shared hardcoded state, no inter-test ordering dependency, no hardcoded secrets/connection strings (grepped both test files). (2) Full-suite failure attribution: did NOT blindly trust TEST-DESIGNER's claim -- ran test/letflow/identity_test.exs myself twice, independently, and reproduced the identical 2 failures both times ('resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 resolves the seeded default tenant (bpm-default)...' and the mirrored 'resolve_realm_by_tenant/1' test), both raising Ecto.NoResultsError at test/support/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex:118 inside `with_lock/1` -- exact match to TEST-DESIGNER's claim. Read that helper's own moduledoc: it explicitly documents this precise cross-OS-process race (two concurrent `mix test` invocations sharing one non-partitioned test DB racing the single migration-seeded 'bpm-default' tenant row) as a previously-reproduced, known class, with a real Postgres advisory-lock mitigation that still has this one narrow window. Confirmed identity_test.exs/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex are untouched by ISS-0771's diff and outside TEST-DESIGNER's owned_modules -- genuinely pre-existing and unrelated, not a regression from this fix. (3) Mandatory mutant re-application (WF-03 'code under test does not exist' rule, since this is 100% new code): applied TEST-DESIGNER's step-06-documented combined mutant 1 myself, first-hand, in a throwaway worktree (`../iss0771-tdv-mutant-check`, created off HEAD 6766956a, removed after use via `git worktree remove --force`) -- removed replay_all_pending/0's outer per-tenant rescue AND changed replay_migrations/1's own Layer-1 rescue clause from `exception -> {:error, {:migration_failed, exception}}` to `exception -> reraise exception, __STACKTRACE__`. Measured myself: 'Finished in 5.1 seconds' / 'Result: 21/23 passed' -- exactly 2 failures, exactly the two isolation-dependent tests ('one tenant's broken schema does not abort replay for a healthy sibling tenant' and 'start_link/1 returns :ignore and logs the failing tenant even when a tenant's replay fails'), matching TEST-DESIGNER's step-06 mutation-testing evidence precisely. Reverted via `git checkout -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex`; verified `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty in the mutant worktree, then reran targeted tests there -> 'Result: 23 passed' again, confirming a clean revert before removing the worktree. This checkout's own `git status --porcelain` shows only this handoff file modified throughout.

issues.description: Independent judgment call on the uncatchable-mutant finding (task's specific ask): the NARROW single-layer mutant re-tested at step-10/11/12 (remove only replay_all_pending/0's outer rescue, leaving replay_migrations/1's Layer-1 rescue intact) is correctly, and unavoidably, uncatchable by any test -- Layer 1 mathematically absorbs every reachable exception before Layer 2 is ever reached, so no test written against real (non-mocked) Postgres could ever observe Layer 2's removal in isolation. This is NOT evidence of a coverage gap, nor is it a fresh open question: TEST-DESIGNER's own step-06 handoff already produced the correct, stronger experiment -- a COMBINED mutant that also breaks Layer 1's rescue (making it reraise instead of returning a tagged tuple) -- and that combined mutant WAS caught (21/23, the 2 Layer-2-dependent tests failing). I reproduced that exact combined-mutant result myself in a throwaway worktree (see result.summary) and got the identical 21/23 split. Conclusion: the outer rescue is proven load-bearing, not decorative or dead code -- it is unreachable only under the narrower, weaker mutant, which is expected given the design's own stated two-layers-in-series architecture. No follow-up needed; TEST-DESIGNER's INFO note undersold this slightly by not cross-referencing step-06's own stronger evidence when re-flagging it at step-12, but did not misstate anything and appropriately deferred the judgment call rather than silently resolving it. Acceptable defense-in-depth, coverage genuinely proven via mutation testing, not merely asserted.

The 2 full-suite failures (test/letflow/identity_test.exs, REQ-019 AC1) are confirmed by me, independently and twice, to be a genuine pre-existing/unrelated flake (documented cross-process race in test/support/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex, a file neither owned by TEST-DESIGNER nor touched by ISS-0771's diff or either mutant). Consistent with TEST-DESIGNER's claim. Worth a separate tracked issue if one does not already exist, but out of scope for this gate and not blocking.
